summary: Turn hotel, transport and supplier emissions into practical reduction actions. Explore the five-day tourism operations course and its applied exercises.
lede: Carbon footprint reduction in tourism operations uses emissions evidence to guide changes to energy, transport, food and purchasing. Designed for intermediate accommodation, tour-operation and sustainability professionals, the course develops skills in setting boundaries with the GHG Protocol, reviewing operational data, comparing HCMI-informed hotel emissions intensity, prioritising reduction measures and defining owners and progress indicators for a cost-aware action plan.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who influence energy, transport, food, procurement or guest-service decisions across accommodation and tour operations. It suits intermediate learners who can bring operational context to emissions-reduction exercises.
modules: Tourism Boundaries with the GHG Protocol
GSTC Criteria for Food and Waste
prerequisites: Working knowledge of tourism operations and familiarity with basic energy, fuel, food-waste or purchasing records are expected. No coding is required. Advanced energy-management and sustainability criteria are introduced at an operational awareness level; the course does not teach implementation or certification.
